Replaice in practice

Where Replaice adds value

Reduce duplicate project administration

Carry site assumptions, drawing revisions and quantities into schedules, trade packages and claims reviews. Teams spend less time copying records and reconciling versions.

Make changes visible across delivery

Use Pulse milestones, Vault revisions and ResourceFlow forecasts to see how a scope change affects procurement dates and crew capacity.

Keep commercial decisions traceable

Review bids against a consistent scope and compare subcontractor claims with awarded rates and prior certifications. Keep award and payment approvals with authorised staff.

BiltFlow lifecycle

From site feasibility to subcontractor payment.

Follow the project records that connect planning, design coordination, procurement and delivery.

  1. 01
    SiteScope

    Scope the site

    Compare feasibility scenarios and capture site constraints.

    HandoffFeasibility assumptions and site constraints

  2. 02

    Build the baseline schedule with phases, dependencies and milestones.

    HandoffMilestones and required-on-site dates

  3. 03
    Vault

    Coordinate drawings and documents

    Create project records and drawing registers. Upload, review, revise and share drawings and documents with controlled access.

    Build packages, issue RFQs, compare bids and award subcontractor contracts.

    Review progress claims against awarded scope, contract terms and program milestones. Certify approved amounts for payment.

Illustrative case study · Australia

A major contractor consolidates its project technology.

This model represents a large Australian contractor running multiple projects. The figures are planning assumptions for a hypothetical rollout.

A$720,000Modelled annual technology savings
30%Lower recurring technology budget
8,000 hoursModelled annual administrative capacity freed

Annual technology budget

Amounts in AUD. The model assumes overlapping tools are retired after rollout.

Cost categoryBeforeAfter
Software subscriptionsA$1.40mA$1.00m
Integrations and maintenanceA$600kA$430k
External technical supportA$400kA$250k
TotalA$2.40mA$1.68m

The model excludes one-off migration and training costs. Administrative capacity is tracked separately from the technology savings.

How agents reduce manual effort

  • Drawing changes. Flag changes for quantity and schedule review. 1,200 reviews × 3 hours saved = 3,600 hours.
  • Procurement packages. Draft scopes from approved quantities and flag gaps in bids. 900 packages × 2 hours saved = 1,800 hours.
  • Subcontractor claims. Check rates and prior claims and route discrepancies to the reviewer. 1,300 claims × 2 hours saved = 2,600 hours.

That is about 4.4 full-time equivalents of capacity at 1,800 productive hours per year. Project teams retain approval of awards and payments and can redirect that time to delivery and exception handling.
